tb/cocotb/bfm/axi4_master.py: restructured AW/AR polling to check ReadOnly of the SAME cycle as the drive (await ReadOnly() first, then await RisingEdge if not seen) — allows catching combinational DECERR awready at T while still catching normal-path awready at T+1; same fix for W-channel polling

tb/cocotb/soc/axi4_slave_model.py: complete rewrite using edge-based handshake: (1) AW/W/AR: assert ready, poll RisingEdge+ReadOnly loop, await RisingEdge after break to deassert in active phase; (2) B/R: assert valid in active phase, poll ReadOnly+RisingEdge loop (check current ReadOnly first to match BFM pattern), await RisingEdge after break; (3) R multi-beat loop: mandatory await RisingEdge at TOP of each beat iteration to guarantee active-phase context before driving rid/rdata/rvalid/rlast
notes: Key lesson: in cocotb with Verilator, the canonical AXI4 handshake pattern for a READY responder is: assert ready (active), poll [await ReadOnly; if valid: break; else: await RisingEdge], then await RisingEdge before deassert. For a VALID initiator: assert valid+data (active), poll [await ReadOnly; if ready: break; else: await RisingEdge], await RisingEdge before deassert. The DECERR engine uses combinational awready (valid only during DW_IDLE, cleared at the same rising edge where aw_unmapped is captured), so the BFM must sample ReadOnly of the drive cycle, not just T+1. Multi-beat loops must start each beat with await RisingEdge to avoid executing signal writes while still in ReadOnly context from the previous beat's break.

BNE branch-offset bug pattern: B-type immediate is PC-relative byte offset. BNE at 0x0C with imm=-8 goes to 0x04 (two instructions back), not 0x08 (one instruction back).
